items.title: Transfer of copyright for “The Young Band Master” by Capt. Ralph Bonehill
items.ocr:
New York, Sept. 26, 1899.

For the sum of $75, a receipt of which is hereby acknowledged, I transfer the copyright of the story "The Young Band Master," by Capt. Ralph Bonehill, to Edward Stratemeyer.

Library of Congress
Washington, D.C.

The accompanying assignment of copyright has been filed in the office of the Librarian of Congress in conformity with the laws of the United States respecting copyright.

items.title: Transfer to Edward Stratemeyer of uncompleted manuscript written by Horatio Alger, Jr.
items.ocr:
Natick, Mass., Nov. 24th, 1899.

For and in consideration of the sum of One Hundred and Fifty Dollars, ($150.), the receipt of which is hereby acknowledged, I, as executrix of the estate of the late Horatio Alger, Jr., do transfer and set aside to Edward Stratemeyer, of Newark, N. J., and his heirs, an uncompleted manuscript written by Horatio Alger, Jr., bearing no name but relating the adventures of a boy called Robert Frost.

With the transfer of this uncompleted manuscript I also give to Edward Stratemeyer the right to divide the manuscript into two parts and then lengthen each part into a book story, so that both completed stories shall form companion volumes. Each of these volumes shall be published as written by Horatio Alger, Jr., and completed by ——— (naming some other author or nom-de-plume of an author).

With this transfer I also give to Edward Stratemeyer the right to dispose of copyrights on the two stories as he may desire. I agree to protect him in all his rights in them and especially in his right to the use of the name of Horatio Alger, Jr., as described above.

In witness I have hereunto affixed my signature, on this day and at the place above mentioned.
